== Biography ==
William is currently recorded as born about 1735, attached as a son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and [[Rutherford-4861|Margaret Rutherford]], and as having died about 1829 in the United States. The cited basis is a user-contributed FamilySearch tree; no inspected original record yet proves those events or relationships.

== Research Notes ==
=== Moneymore place conflict ===

The structured birthplace “Moneymore, Galway, Connacht” combines a real place-name with a county that does not fit the Moneymore used in this family reconstruction. Moneymore in Artrea civil parish is in County Londonderry, not County Galway.<ref>[https://www.townlands.ie/londonderry/loughinsholin/artrea/moneymore/moneymore/ Townlands.ie, “Moneymore Townland, Co. Londonderry”], placing Moneymore in Artrea civil parish, barony of Loughinsholin, County Londonderry.</ref> This geographic correction does '''not''' prove that William was born in the Londonderry townland: several Irish places share the name, and no record inspected for William identifies one of them.

PRONI's official church-register guide lists First Moneymore Presbyterian baptisms only from 1827, Second Moneymore from 1845, and Ardtrea/Desertlin Roman Catholic baptisms from 1832.<ref>[https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Guide to Church Records''], First Moneymore Presbyterian MIC1P/339; Second Moneymore Presbyterian MIC1P/340; Ardtrea/Desertlin MIC1D/35 and T3050; guide consulted 30 August 2026.</ref> None of those surviving series can record a birth about 1735. This explains the register gap but does not prove William's identity, birthplace or parents; deeds, estate papers, probate and other contemporary records remain the appropriate next search.

The current parents, sibling group, birth and death locations and estimated years are retained until evidence supplies replacements. They should be treated as unproved tree claims, as noted in [[Space:Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland|Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland]], rather than silently cleared or converted into a different family.

=== Possible William Glascoe, Maryland notice ===
A Lancaster Goal notice dated 13 October says John M’Connel, about 35, imprisoned as a suspected runaway servant, claims to belong to William Glascoe in Maryland, about forty miles from Baltimore.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39392109/ Pennsylvania Gazette, 1775-10-25, p.1].</ref>

The Maryland location is John M’Connel’s attributed claim, not independently proved residence. The notice gives no relatives for William or evidence that he was the 1760 London defendant.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2426]]. William’s estimated 1735 birth and later American context are chronologically compatible, but no record places him at the stated Maryland location.

=== Possible William Glasgow, Philadelphia and Charles-Town postal lists, 1759–1771 ===
William Glasgow, Cecil County, is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39399295/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1759-08-09, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in February 1763.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39390517/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1763-02-24, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in October 1765.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39405824/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1765-10-10, p.4].</ref>

William Glasgow is separately listed in the Charles-Town, Maryland, post-office letters notice headed 1 October 1771, beside an entry for John Glasgow of West Nottingham.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41041559/ Maryland Gazette, 1771-10-24, p.3].</ref>

Cecil County explicitly qualifies the 1759 entry only. In 1763 "Pennsylvania" follows James Gillispie; in 1765 "Forks of Delaware" qualifies William Greenlee, not William Glasgow. The entries may concern different men, and co-listing with John in 1771 does not prove a family relationship.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2426]]. Estimated 1735 birth and later United States context are unproved family account; no postal identification. The Moneymore County Galway field is disputed.
